title: Simple TODO Application — React Frontend + Express Backend + SQLite
problem_statement: Users need a simple, reliable way to capture, organize, and track daily tasks. Without a dedicated task management tool, tasks get lost in chat messages, sticky notes, or mental memory, leading to missed deadlines and reduced productivity. This application provides a focused, local-first TODO list where users can quickly add, edit, complete, and remove tasks — with all data persisted durably in SQLite, requiring no external database server or cloud dependency.
target_users: Individual users managing personal daily tasks
Professionals tracking work items and action items
Students organizing assignments and study tasks
Developers who want a zero-dependency local task tracker

functional_requirements.description: View the full list of TODO items on page load
acceptance_criteria: On page load, the frontend fetches GET /api/tasks and renders all tasks
Each task displays its title, description (if present), completion status, and creation date
An empty-state message is shown when no tasks exist (e.g., 'No tasks yet — create one above!')
The list re-renders automatically after any add, edit, toggle, or delete operation

functional_requirements.description: Create a new TODO item with a required title and optional description
acceptance_criteria: An input form provides fields for title (required) and description (optional)
Submitting via button click or Enter key sends POST /api/tasks with the task payload
The new task appears in the list immediately on success
Empty or whitespace-only titles are rejected with a client-side validation message
The input field is cleared after successful creation
Duplicate submissions are prevented (submit button disabled while request is in-flight)

functional_requirements.description: Toggle a task's completion status (mark done / mark undone)
acceptance_criteria: Each task row includes a checkbox or toggle for completion status
Clicking the toggle sends PUT /api/tasks/:id with the flipped completed boolean
The UI updates optimistically and reverts if the server request fails
Completed tasks are visually distinct (strikethrough title, muted text color)
Toggling a completed task back to incomplete restores its normal visual state

functional_requirements.description: Delete a TODO item with a confirmation step
acceptance_criteria: Each task row includes a delete action (trash icon or button)
Clicking delete triggers a confirmation prompt before proceeding
On confirmation, DELETE /api/tasks/:id is called and the task is removed from the list
If the server request fails, the task remains visible and an error is shown
Canceling the confirmation leaves the task untouched

functional_requirements.description: Edit an existing task's title and description inline
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a task title or an edit button enters inline edit mode
In edit mode, title and description become editable text inputs
Pressing Enter or clicking Save sends PUT /api/tasks/:id with the updated fields
Pressing Escape or clicking Cancel exits edit mode and restores original values
Saving an empty title is rejected with validation

functional_requirements.description: Filter tasks by completion status (All / Active / Completed)
acceptance_criteria: Filter tabs or buttons offer three views: All, Active (incomplete), Completed
The active filter is visually highlighted
Filtering can be done client-side from already-fetched data for responsiveness
The filter state persists across operations (newly added tasks appear under the correct filter)

functional_requirements.description: RESTful API provides task CRUD endpoints backed by SQLite
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/tasks — returns JSON array of all tasks, ordered by created_at DESC
GET /api/tasks?status=active|completed — returns filtered tasks
GET /api/tasks/:id — returns a single task object or 404
POST /api/tasks — accepts { title: string, description?: string }, returns 201 with created task
PUT /api/tasks/:id — accepts partial update { title?, description?, completed? }, returns updated task or 404
DELETE /api/tasks/:id — deletes task, returns 204 on success or 404
All endpoints validate input and return consistent JSON error responses: { error: string } with appropriate HTTP status codes (400, 404, 500)

functional_requirements.description: The application handles API and network errors gracefully
acceptance_criteria: Network errors (timeout, server unreachable) display a user-friendly error message
Failed mutations show an error toast/notification without crashing the app
Optimistic UI updates are rolled back if the server request fails
A retry mechanism or manual retry button is offered for failed fetch operations

non_functional_requirements.description: API response time for single-task CRUD operations
non_functional_requirements.threshold: p95 < 50ms for local SQLite reads; p95 < 100ms for writes

non_functional_requirements.description: Frontend initial page load and first paint
non_functional_requirements.threshold: First Contentful Paint < 1.5s; task list visible < 2s on localhost

non_functional_requirements.description: UI responsiveness for task list rendering
non_functional_requirements.threshold: List of 1,000 tasks renders without visible jank (< 16ms frame budget)

non_functional_requirements.description: Data durability — tasks must survive server restart and page refresh
non_functional_requirements.threshold: Zero data loss on clean shutdown; SQLite WAL journal mode enabled for crash resilience
Usable at viewport widths from 320px (mobile) to 1920px+ (desktop)

non_functional_requirements.description: Keyboard accessibility for all core operations
non_functional_requirements.threshold: Add, toggle, edit, and delete operations fully operable via keyboard alone (Tab, Enter, Escape, Space)
WCAG 2.1 Level AA — proper ARIA labels, focus management, color contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1 for text

non_functional_requirements.description: Input validation and SQL injection prevention
non_functional_requirements.threshold: All API inputs validated; parameterized SQL queries only (no string concatenation); XSS prevention via React's default escaping

non_functional_requirements.description: HTTP security headers on the Express server
non_functional_requirements.threshold: Helmet middleware or equivalent configured with appropriate CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options headers

non_functional_requirements.description: Task volume the application can handle without degradation
non_functional_requirements.threshold: 10,000 tasks stored in SQLite; list rendering performs acceptably (consider virtualization above 1,000 visible rows)

constraints: Frontend must be built with React (JavaScript or TypeScript)
Backend must be built with Node.js and Express.js
Database must be SQLite, using a file-based database (e.g., better-sqlite3 or sqlite3 npm package)
The frontend and backend communicate exclusively via RESTful JSON API
The full stack must run locally — no cloud services, no external database server
No authentication or multi-user support in the initial version (single-user local app)
Must work in modern browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (latest 2 versions)
Setup must be minimal: clone repo, install dependencies, run start command
assumptions: The application is single-user; no authentication, authorization, or user accounts
SQLite database file is stored locally (e.g., ./data/todos.db in the project directory)
SQLite is configured with WAL journal mode for better concurrent read performance

Task data model: id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT), title (TEXT NOT NULL), description (TEXT, nullable), completed (INTEGER/BOOLEAN DEFAULT 0), created_at (TEXT/DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP), updated_at (TEXT/DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
The backend runs on port 3001; the React dev server on port 3000 with a proxy to 3001 for /api routes
Node.js (v18+) and npm are pre-installed on the user's machine
Task titles are plain text — no Markdown rendering, rich text, or file attachments
No real-time sync, WebSockets, or collaboration features are needed
TypeScript is optional; if used, it applies to both frontend and backend consistently

clarifying_questions.question: Should tasks support additional fields beyond title, description, and completion status — such as due date, priority level (high/medium/low), or tags/categories?
Should tasks be reorderable via drag-and-drop, or is sorting by creation date (newest first) sufficient?
Is there a need for data export/import functionality (e.g., export all tasks as JSON or CSV)?
Should the app support dark mode / theme toggling in the initial release?
Is there a preferred UI styling approach — plain CSS, CSS Modules, Tailwind CSS, or a component library like Material UI?
Should the app be containerized (Docker) or packaged (Electron) for distribution, or is running via npm scripts sufficient?
